answer.text: Market participants and investors generally, including individuals and groups
No one - markets are fully rational

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats behavioural finance as the study of how psychological factors influence market participants and investors generally, at the level of both individuals and groups. The biases discussed (anchoring, herding, overconfidence, loss aversion, and so on) are presented as broadly applicable, not limited to a particular investor segment. The Trap: "Only retail investors" and "Only foreign institutional investors" both wrongly carve out a single investor class. "No one - markets are fully rational" is the strict efficient-markets view that the behavioural-finance chapter is written precisely to qualify. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), pp. 240-247 (behavioural finance and biases) and p. 209.
